sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.5403 Of 2019
Order:

The petitioners/A2 to A6 seek to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.284 of 2019 of Pattabhipuram Police Station, Guntur District, which was taken cognizance for the offences under Sections 188, 272, 273, 328, 420 of IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act (for short, 'FSS Act').

2. The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that on 25.08.2019 at about 4:30 p.m., when the complainant along with his staff, on credible information, rushed to 5th lane, Devapuram, Near Pattabhi Seetharamaiah School, Guntur, found the A1, who sold gutkha and khaini packets, seized the same, arrested him and registered a case in Crime No.284 of 2019 for the offences stated supra.
Later, the petitioners were added as A2 to A6 in the above said case.

3. Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto basing on the report of the S.I of Police, Pattabhipuram Police Station.
Therefore, it is the violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

5. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioners/A2 to A6 under Sections 188, 272, 273, 328,
420 of IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of FSS Act are hereby quashed.
